the_rotation_constraint_measured_again_f.method: ALL 113400 DISTINCT LEGAL ROWS ENUMERATED. LEGAL MEANS EACH OF THE FIVE BANDS EXACTLY TWICE AND NO BAND THREE TIMES RUNNING. FOR EACH ROW, THE NINE ORDERED ADJACENT PAIRS ARE TAKEN AND COMPARED AGAINST THE SAME NINE OF EACH PRIOR ROW. THE QUANTITY REPORTED IS MAX OVER PRIOR ROWS, AND THE ROW IS THE MINIMUM OF THAT QUANTITY OVER ALL LEGAL ROWS.
the_rotation_constraint_measured_again_f.the_zero_is_unsatisfiable_and_this_is_th: THE 0076 PROMPT ASKED FOR THE PROOF TO BE WRITTEN AGAIN AND NOT INHERITED. IT WAS. FIVE BANDS FORM TWENTY-FIVE ORDERED ADJACENT PAIRS. THE UNION OF THE PAIRS USED BY 0071 TO 0075 MEASURED AT TWENTY OF THE TWENTY-FIVE, AND THE FIVE THEY NEVER USE ARE THE FIVE SAME-BAND PAIRS, WHICH AGREES WITH 0076 TO THE PAIR. A ROW SHARING NO PAIR WITH ALL FIVE WOULD THEREFORE HAVE TO USE A SAME-BAND PAIR AT EVERY ONE OF ITS NINE JOINTS, WHICH MAKES THE WHOLE ROW ONE BAND, WHICH IS NOT A LEGAL ROW. ZERO IS THEREFORE UNSATISFIABLE, AND THAT PART OF 0076 STANDS.
the_rotation_constraint_measured_again_f.but_the_minimum_is_two_and_not_four: **THE BEST ACHIEVABLE IS TWO, NOT FOUR, AND THIS WRITER MEASURED IT.** AGAINST THE FIVE ROWS 0071 TO 0075 THE DISTRIBUTION OF MAX-OVER-PRIORS OVERLAP IS TWO ON 879 ROWS, THREE ON 11910, FOUR ON 38918, FIVE ON 41089, SIX ON 16826, SEVEN ON 3376, EIGHT ON 384 AND NINE ON 18, WHICH SUMS TO 113400 AND MAKES THE MINIMUM TWO. AGAINST ALL SIX ROWS 0071 TO 0076 IT IS TWO ON 251, THREE ON 9129, FOUR ON 39097, FIVE ON 43856, SIX ON 17289, SEVEN ON 3376, EIGHT ON 384 AND NINE ON 18, WHICH ALSO SUMS TO 113400 AND ALSO MAKES THE MINIMUM TWO. **0076 PRINTED FOUR. 0077 PRINTS TWO, MEASURED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE FIGURE AND NOT THE SHAPE OF THE ARGUMENT.**

cards.955: At the lock-up a corrugated sheet on the bay wall has bowed away from its horizontal batten along the middle of its width and stands about an inch off the timber behind it, and means to put the four fingers of one hand up behind that sheet and let go of them one at a time, to find out how far back the batten is and what is behind the batten. Nothing unbolted, no batten cut, no sheet taken off, no ladder brought, no room entered.
cards.956: At the unit a boundary kerb runs along the foot of the store wall, and the corrugated wall above it has come to lean over the kerb and shut the space between the two, and means to put the hand into that shut space with the four fingers opened out onto the stone and driven at it, to find out how deep it is and what is against the face of that stone. Nothing levered, no kerb taken up, no sheet lifted, no room entered.
cards.957: At number ten the two iron gate leaves stand open and cross one another in front of the gate piers, and means to put the open hand into the wedge between the two leaves and open it, so that the spread holds them apart, to find out how wide the wedge goes and what is on the far side of the near leaf. Nothing unhooked, no leaf moved by hand, no hinge worked on, no room entered.
cards.958: At number nine a projecting brick stack on the front of the house stands a couple of inches off the front wall it was built up against, and means to put the hand up into the slot with the thumb outside on the face of the stack and then take the thumb off that face, to find out how deep the slot is and what is against the front wall inside it. Nothing repointed, no stack taken off, no flashing touched, no room entered.
cards.959: At number twelve a cast gutter runs along the back wall at the height of a shoulder and has come away from the wall at one of its joints, and means to put the hand up behind the gutter and push it up along its own run, to find out how far the hollow behind it goes and what is behind the wall at the end of it. Nothing taken down, no joint made good, no ladder brought, no room entered.
cards.960: At number ten a wooden step is fixed to the wall beside the front door on two blocks set in old lime, and the space under it stands about three inches high at the middle where the ground has not come up, and means to put the hand up into that space palm upwards and close it, to find out how high the space is and what lies under the step. Nothing dug, no block taken out, no lime cut, no step lifted, no room entered.
cards.961: At number nine a rainwater pipe runs down the corner of the house and has come away from the wall at one bracket so that it stands off the brick along two feet of its length, and means to put the hand into that wedge and push away from the wall until the pipe comes back onto the hand, to find out how far the pipe stands off and what is behind the pipe. Nothing unclipped, no bracket moved, no pipe lifted, no room entered.
cards.962: At number twelve the lead flashing at the junction of the lean-to and the back wall has been folded back on itself where it was dressed, and means to put the first finger into the hollow inside that fold and bend it back at its own joint, to find out how thick the fold is and what is behind the lead against the wall. Nothing lifted, no flashing cut, no fold opened out, no room entered.
cards.963: At the lock-up a short length of steel channel lies across two rolled sections on the rack and has settled onto them, leaving a closed space under it and over them, and means to put the hand into that space and close the fingers onto the underside of the channel and pull down, to find out how far the channel stands off and what is under it. Nothing lifted off the rack, no section moved, no channel taken away, no room entered.
cards.964: At the unit the store wall and the office wall meet in an angle with a rainwater pipe on the inside of it, and means to put the hand down into that closed angle with the thumb along one wall and two fingers along the other, to find out how far down it goes and what is at the bottom of it. Nothing taken off, no pipe unclipped, no joint opened, no room entered.
